title: Why sangha
hook: the whole of the holy life is good friendship (SN 45.2)
tomorrow: how did one rich man find the Buddha in the dark?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a yearly pilgrimage: a place to go, chosen because it wakes you up. Today, the people you walk with.
screen: `A PLACE TO GO.` → `THE PEOPLE YOU WALK WITH.`

segments.voice: Some people only make it to the gym because a friend texts at six: you up? Others swear they do their best work alone, headphones in. Mai is the second kind. After Thursday's sit, the people there asked her to stay for tea and a reading circle, and she'd rather get back to the studio. She knows the sutta she read with Ava: Ananda calls good friendship half the holy life, and the Buddha says no, it's the whole. But the same canon keeps a second voice. And it sounds a lot like Mai.
screen: `A FRIEND WHO TEXTS AT SIX.` → `OR HEADPHONES IN, ALONE.` → `A SECOND VOICE IN THE CANON.`

segments.voice: An old poem in the Sutta Nipata keeps coming back to one refrain: wander alone, like the rhinoceros. Its case is strong. Company brings attachment, quarrels, other people's moods. Alone, nobody pulls you off course, and nobody's opinion becomes your path. Now the other voice. Good friendship, the Buddha tells Ananda, is the whole of the holy life, because someone with good friends can be expected to walk the path. The Pali word is kalyanamitta, a good, lovely friend, and he names himself as one: it's by having him as a good friend that beings are freed. Both are scripture. So which is it? Listen closer, because the poem doesn't disagree as much as it seems. In the middle of it, it says: if you find a wise companion, someone steady who lives well, walk with them, glad and mindful. Only if you find no such friend, go alone. So the real question is which company. That's why Buddhists name the sangha, the community, as one of the three refuges, beside the Buddha and the teaching. Not any crowd. The friends who help you keep walking.
screen: `THE RHINOCEROS: WANDER ALONE.` · `GOOD FRIENDSHIP: THE WHOLE.` · `UNLESS YOU FIND A WISE COMPANION.` · `SANGHA, ONE OF THE THREE REFUGES.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE OF IT.`

segments.voice: Think of one person who makes a good habit of yours easier to keep: the one who shows up, who asks how it's going. Write them a short message telling them so. Send it now or later, your choice, and sit with their face in mind while the sit runs.
Why sangha: because good friends, the Buddha told Ananda, aren't half of the holy life. They're all of it.
Your line: the whole of it. Alone if you must, with a wise friend if you can. Fourteen days into the block.

howItsDone: Buddhists take refuge in the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Sangha, often reciting the three refuges together at a temple or group sit; monks and nuns live in community, and lay Buddhists meet in temple groups and sitting groups.

fork.setup: Mai says she practices best alone; her friend says you can't grow without a group. give the rhinoceros poem's best case, in a sentence.

fork.reveal: that's the poem's real case: company brings ties and moods. and the same poem adds: if you find a wise companion, walk with them.

tie.story: The rhinoceros poem praises wandering alone, yet says to walk with a wise companion if you find one; the Buddha called good friendship the whole.

Ananda.meaning: the Buddha's cousin and close attendant

kalyanamitta.meaning: a good, lovely friend on the path

Sutta Nipata.meaning: an early collection of Buddhist poems and discourses

sangha.meaning: the community on the path; one of the three refuges

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 45.2 (Upaddha Sutta: half the holy life)
Sutta Nipata 1.3 (Khaggavisana Sutta, the rhinoceros), the verses on a wise companion

notes: SN 45.2 paraphrased: Ananda says good friendship is half the holy life; the Buddha says not so, it is the whole, a monk with good friends can be expected to develop the eightfold path, and by relying on him as a good friend beings subject to birth are freed. Confirm.

Sutta Nipata 1.3 paraphrased (refrain: wander alone like a rhinoceros; the verses that say if one finds a prudent, steady companion one should walk with him, glad and mindful, and only otherwise alone). Whether the refrain means the rhinoceros or its single horn is debated; the script says 'like the rhinoceros'. Confirm.
Trapdoor floor 3: in the suttas sangha usually refers to the monastic or noble-disciple community; the broader use for any practice group is modern. Confirm wording.

Shape: debate (two views inside the canon, both allowed to speak; the fork asks for the other side's best case). Mai's storyline: the Thursday sit near her summer program (from day 1731) asks her to stay for tea and a reading circle. Day 1724 already taught SN 45.2's 'not half, the whole' as Mai and Ava's reading; this day takes a new angle (the rhinoceros poem as the second voice) and recalls 1724 in the hook.
Surprising fact: the poem famous for 'wander alone' itself says to walk with a wise companion if you find one.
